text_blocks.snippet: While most side effects from COVID-19 vaccines are mild and temporary, some serious, though rare, adverse events have been reported, including myocarditis, pericarditis, and thrombotic events. These events are rare and occur in a small percentage of individuals receiving the vaccines.

list.title: Myocarditis and Pericarditis:
list.snippet: These are inflammations of the heart muscle and the lining around the heart, respectively. They are more commonly reported in younger males, particularly after the second dose of mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna).

list.title: Thrombosis with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (TTS):
list.snippet: This rare condition involves blood clots and low platelet counts. It has been associated with the adenovirus vector vaccines (Johnson & Johnson/Janssen).
Acute Coronary Syndrome: A range of conditions including heart attack.
Cardiac Arrest: The heart stops beating.
Anemia: A deficiency in red blood cells.

text_blocks.snippet: Common Side Effects (generally mild and temporary):
Fatigue, Headache, Muscle pain, Chills, Fever, and Injection site pain.

Important Note: The benefits of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death far outweigh the risks of these rare adverse events. If you experience any unusual symptoms after vaccination, it's crucial to seek medical attention.
